verdict: Oracle's revenue rose 7% to $13.3B as cloud revenue grew 25%, and its backlog of signed contracts jumped 29% to a record $80B on demand for AI data-center capacity.

segments.name: Cloud services & license support
segments.note: Renting Oracle's cloud, plus support for the software customers already run — the steady base of the business, and three-quarters of all revenue.

segments.name: Cloud license & on-premise license
segments.note: New software licenses sold outright, for customers running Oracle on their own machines.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software — up 5% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, down 6% YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge, down 15% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Acquisition-related costs of $155M plus restructuring charges of $90M.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $876M on Oracle's debt pile, plus $9M of other non-operating expenses, net.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The backlog hit a record
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — work customers have signed for but Oracle has not yet delivered — jumped 29% to over $80B, an all-time record, as large new cloud infrastructure contracts reserved AI capacity. Oracle expects 43% of it to be recognized as revenue over the next four quarters.

takeaways.title: Cloud infrastructure is the engine
takeaways.text: Cloud revenue (IaaS plus SaaS) rose 25% to $5.1B, with cloud infrastructure revenue up 49% to $1.8B and cloud applications up 14% to $3.3B — while total revenue rose 7% to $13.3B.

takeaways.title: GAAP margins widened
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income rose 15% to $3.75B — a 28% operating margin, up from 26% a year ago — and net income rose 27% to $2.40B. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.41, up 16%.

footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud services and license support', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue. Segment names follow the presentation Oracle used through fiscal 2025; from fiscal 2026 Oracle regrouped its reporting into Cloud, Software, Hardware and Services.
